research_strategy.reason: All 21 prior hypotheses failed purely for infrastructural reasons (missing imports, contract mismatches, stale-artifact refusal, smoke-test shape mismatches, or 'not_implementable' verdicts for unsupported dynamics types or history inputs). No scientific evidence is available against any mechanism. We therefore introduce three genuinely new operator constructions that have not appeared in any prior attempt: (1) a graph-Laplacian-structured linear operator with a learnable sparse adjacency (a fundamentally different inductive bias — graph topology — from the dense or POD-banded structures previously tried), (2) a matrix-exponential parameterization of a continuous-time generator (a non-Euclidean parameterization, never explored here, that guarantees invertibility and exposes a natural multi-step rollout), and (3) a mass-conserving diffusion-reaction operator with an explicit 26-26 reactant/product block split (combines a hard conservation constraint with an explicit reaction term, a combination not present in any prior hypothesis, including the symplectic C002_H01 which used a much stronger single-form conservation). All three are compatible with the currently supported dynamics types (linear_operator for H1/H2, residual_operator for H3), with required_history=0, and with the 52D POD-latent contract, so they avoid the previous 'not_implementable' failure mode. They are mutually discriminable by qualitative spectral properties (real vs. complex spectrum; positive determinant; mass conservation), which the baseline single global linear operator cannot simultaneously exhibit.
